All 16 units re-verified against their own C#: 15 are StackType.Single, and NONE overrides InstanceType (PowerModel.cs:144 default None), so none needs T1's instance machinery instead of amount-adding. AfterDeath.maps_to: powers.py:3896-3903 AdaptablePower.on_death, fired from the DEATH (real) arm of cmds._resolve_death (cmds.py:114-122)
AfterDeath.rationale: STALE as filed. RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30: the record's premise ('powers.py:3548-3553 still implements this via should_die returning False, so the sim runs the PREVENTION arm') no longer matches the source. The live AdaptablePower class (powers.py:3862-3911) has no should_die override at all, and its own comment on should_remove_from_combat_after_death says so explicitly: 'There is no ShouldDie override, so the Test Subject really dies and is merely kept in the combat. See IllusionPower.' EXECUTED: grep -rn "def should_die\b" sts2_rl/ -> exactly 2 hits, hooks.py:1196 (the dispatcher) and potions.py:1337 (Fairy in a Bottle); zero in powers.py. So a Test Subject kill now runs _resolve_death's DEATH arm (cmds.py:114-122) -- the REAL-death arm in C# too (CreatureCmd.cs:505-537, taken because AdaptablePower has no ShouldDie override on the C# side either): matching, not diverging. hooks.on_death(target, False) fires (cmds.py:121), so AdaptablePower.on_death's `if was_removal_prevented or creature is not self.owner: return` (powers.py:3900-3901) sees was_removal_prevented=False, mirroring C#'s `if (!wasRemovalPrevented && creature == base.Owner && ...)` (AdaptablePower.cs:34) exactly -- both arm is_reviving/isReviving and call trigger_dead_state/TriggerDeadState on the same condition. GremlinHorn's payout and Feed's `if target.is_dead` scoring both still hold. The 'Test Subject keeps Enrage' claim is now also false: the death arm calls _strip_powers_after_death(hooks, target) unconditionally (cmds.py:122), the sim's port of creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath() (CreatureCmd.cs:530-533), so Enrage (default should_power_be_removed_after_owner_death -> True) is stripped exactly as in C#, while AdaptablePower itself (override -> False) survives, also exactly as in C#. VERIFIED by reading cmds.py:102-155, powers.py:3862-3911, AdaptablePower.cs and IllusionPower.cs in full; IllusionPower's own comment (mirrored at powers.py:1891-1898) documents the identical should_die -> should_remove_from_combat_after_death migration for the sibling power, corroborating that this was a deliberate already-landed engine fix rather than a coincidence.

ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.maps_to: powers.py:3890-3894 AdaptablePower.should_remove_from_combat_after_death, consulted at cmds.py:118-120 on the death arm
ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.rationale: STALE as filed. Settled independently of the AfterDeath entry above by executing this witness itself (per the brief), not by inheriting its label: the premise ('this power still does not implement it') is false. AdaptablePower.should_remove_from_combat_after_death (powers.py:3890-3894) reads `return creature is not self.owner`, which is ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath (AdaptablePower.cs:58-65: `if (creature != base.Owner) return true; return false;`) read line for line. And it is genuinely consulted now: _resolve_death's death arm sets `target.retained_after_death = not hooks.should_remove_from_combat_after_death(target)` (cmds.py:118-120), the sim's port of Hook.ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath(combatState, creature) gating shouldRemoveFromCombat at CreatureCmd.cs:507. So the Test Subject IS retained via this hook, not via an unconditional prevention-arm flag as the stale text claimed -- the prevention arm is not even reached (see the AfterDeath entry and the g5 guard). VERIFIED by reading powers.py:3862-3911 and cmds.py:102-136 together.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath.rationale: `ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath() => false`. C# strips a dead creature's powers at CreatureCmd.cs:533 (`creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath()`, then each power's AfterRemoved) and this override opts out so the power survives the death it is supposed to react to. The sim never removes powers on death at all -- a grep of cmds.py's kill/death path finds no `powers.clear()` or per-power removal, and cmds.py:96-105 goes straight from the HP write to should_die / should_remove_from_combat_after_death / on_death -- so `false` is the sim's universal behaviour and this override is satisfied for free. Faithful HERE. The inverse is a real machinery gap owned by nobody: the C# DEFAULT is `true`, so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is. That is reported in content-power-report-b.md section 3 rather than verdicted on this unit, because it is an engine-wide absence and not this power's divergence. Third-file citations, not hashed here. ENGINE-LEVEL SIBLING (added 2026-07-26): the INVERSE finding -- that C#'s DEFAULT is `true` so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is -- now carries a verdict of its own at audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 8b (`gap`, LIVE, executed on the Decimillipede). It used to exist only as prose in content-power-report-b.md section 3c. This entry stays `faithful` because the override asks for exactly the behaviour the sim gives for free; the engine-wide absence is step 8b's, not this unit's.

guards.what: The prevention branch's HP contract: sim `hp = 1` vs C# leaving the creature at 0 and re-entering KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition
guards.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27. THE FLOOR IS GONE: `_resolve_death`'s prevention arm (cmds.py:51-64) no longer writes `target.hp = 1`; it leaves the creature dead at 0 HP, sets `retained_after_death = True`, fires `on_death(..., True)` and then `after_preventing_death` -- CreatureCmd.cs:560-571's shape. The 1-vs-0 HP number conformance asserts on now matches, and the downstream consequences this entry listed go with it (Feed's `if target.is_dead` scores, and steam_eruption's HP restore no longer depends on the floor -- it moved to `on_death`, powers.py:2144-2151). WHAT REMAINS: the sim still does not model C#'s RE-ENTRY. CreatureCmd.cs:562-565 re-enters `KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition(creature, force, recursion + 1)` while `creature.IsDead`, up to 10 times before throwing InvalidOperationException; `_resolve_death`'s else-arm simply returns. So a prevention that heals nothing is permanent in the sim and re-kills in the game, and the sim still cannot express a prevention that fails. VERIFIED by reading cmds.py:30-64.
